procedure: Arrange two glass funnels with their narrow ends aligned, and join them securely with adhesive tape to make the sandclock model.
Place the two lids over the wide ends of the funnels; leave the upper lid off while adding dry sand.
Add dry sand to the upper funnel and close it with the lid.
Turn the sandclock so the sand is in the upper funnel and start the stopwatch as the sand begins to flow.
Observe how much time it takes for the sand to flow down completely, and record the time.
Repeat the timing and calculate the average time for a complete flow.
Make a paper scale from the observed sand levels at recorded time intervals and paste it on the glass funnels along the straight side.
aim: To make a model sandclock and measure the time taken for the sand to flow down completely.

viva.question: What is the working principle of a sandclock?
viva.answer: Dry sand flows through a narrow opening under gravity.

viva.question: What starts and stops the timed interval in this activity?
viva.answer: The interval starts when the sand begins to flow and ends when it has flowed down completely.

viva.question: Why should the sand be dry?
viva.answer: Dry sand flows more freely and consistently.

viva.question: Why is the time measured more than once?
viva.answer: Repeated measurements help reduce the effect of random error.

diagram: Draw two funnels joined narrow-end to narrow-end with adhesive tape, sand in the upper funnel and collected sand in the lower funnel; label the upper funnel, lower funnel, dry sand, direction of sand flow, adhesive tape, lids, and paper scale.
title: Model of a Sandclock
precautions: Join the funnel ends securely so that sand cannot leak out.
Keep the sandclock upright and do not shake it while timing.
Start and stop the stopwatch carefully at the beginning and end of the flow.
Keep the model on a stable surface while marking the scale.
result: The model sandclock was made successfully. The average time for the sand to flow down completely was 42 s.
